title: Why Do Cats PURR? 🐱
description:
You scratch your cat and she purrs... happy cat, right? Maybe. Cats purr when they're content, but also when they're hurt, frightened or hungry, so scientists think a purr is less "I'm happy" and more "look after me". Subscribe for a new strange question every day.

How it works: a cat's voice box flutters about 25 times a second while she breathes in AND out, so the sound never stops for breath. (A 2023 study found soft pads in the vocal folds that let them vibrate that slowly; how much the throat muscles drive each flutter is still debated.) Kittens start purring within days of birth, before their eyes open. And when a cat wants food, she slips a higher cry into the purr, at 220 to 520 Hz, close to a human baby's cry (300 to 600 Hz): in a 2009 study, people rated those purrs as more urgent, even people who had never owned a cat. The popular idea that purring heals bones has not been proven.
